newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar's yen rally falters, Eurostocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar's yen rally falters, Eurostocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar's rally against the yen faltered by mid-afternoon in Europe on Thursday, while European stock markets gained some support but remained mixed after Wall Street opened firmer.
The dollar charged higher to stand near to 116 yen in early European trade, more than two yen up from late Wednesday, as Japanese and U.S. officials continued to will the U.S. currency higher.
"The comments by the Japanese that the yen has gone too far and too fast and rates are not going up are finally filtering through," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London.
The Japanese government has been battling to give the dollar a leg-up after it sank to five-month lows of 111.88 yen on Tuesday on expectations that Japan may soon raise interest rates.
The dollar stood at 115.65 yen at around 1400 GMT against 113.65 in late Europe on Wednesday.

"Certainly, Japanese policymakers appear keen to inject a note of calm into the market, and speculation about an imminent rate hike from the BoJ (Bank of Japan) also appears to be abating," said Paul Meggyesi, currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts said the dollar also appeared well bid after finding a floor below 112 yen earlier this week. "The comments have become a bit more urgent," said Ferridge.

In the latest round of verbal intervention, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said it agreed with the BoJ's low interest-rate policy and that concerns about excessive yen weakness were now completely gone.
Earlier, Takashini Anzai, executive director of the BoJ, said: "Correction to the yen's excessive weakness has begun, but the pace has been too rapid."
Some support for the ailing dollar also came after U.S. Trade Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated the U.S. strong-dollar policy.
But the dollar was more than a pfennig down from highs above 1.70 marks at 1400 GMT in Europe, when it stood at 1.6885.
Wall Street's opening gains, which carried it 14.01 points higher in the first 30 minutes of trading although it later retreated, gave European shares an initial boost.
Prices in London and Paris both started the day lower, but while London then rallied Paris fell further. German shares opened higher before turning lower.

By mid-afternoon London's FTSE index was up 19.2 points at 4,661.2, while in Paris the CAC blue-chip index was down 33.80 points, or 1.21 percent at 2,752.55. Germany's 30-share DAX index ended down 16.67 points at 3,579.42 points after earlier reaching a new record of 3,616.54.
London's FTSE 100 reversed early losses after data showing strong consumer demand and economic growth cheered the market, dealers and strategists said.

"People have accepted the fact that rates are going to go up and now they think that the sooner rates are raised the more chance of keeping inflation under control. In that way the figures were reasonably positive," said a senior dealer.
Britain's April retail sales rose a monthly 0.1 percent and yearly 4.7 percent against expectations of a monthly 0.3 percent and a yearly 4.1 percent.
First quarter GDP rose 0.9 percent quarterly and three percent on a yearly basis versus a forecast of 1.0 percent quarterly and matching expectations of three percent yearly.

French shares cut their losses after Wall Street opened higher. Traders said the market was down due to profit-taking on the eve of the end of the May trading month on Friday. The May account saw the CAC-40 set a new high of 2,804 points.
Dealers also said there were political worries ahead of this weekend's first round in the parliamentary election.
German shares gave up early gains and ended lower after being hurt by weakness in German debt markets which capped the advance and prompted the share market sell-off, traders said.
"The losses are due to the debt market," said one trader. "It's hard to understand why both markets are falling."

Bund market traders said squabbling over plans to plug the expected 1997 deficit hole was giving both international and domestic investors an uncomfortable feeling about the German market since no clear strategy had emerged.

The losses came despite a report by the Ifo economic research institute that fuelled hopes of stronger German growth without inflation. The institute's April west German business climate index rose to 94.07 from 92.6 in March.

"This is of course a really good number," said Gernot Nerb, senior economist at Salomon Brothers. "I would expect that mainly the export sector has boosted the index because construction and retailing remains sluggish.
The Bundesbank also announced M3 money supply grew an annualised 6.7 percent in April versus the average for the fourth quarter of 1996, lower than market expectations.
But the German debt market failed to get a boost from the M3 data, the Bundesbank's main economic benchmark, and traded lower, putting a cap on share market gains.
STOCK PRICES AT 1400 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 19.2 points at 4,661.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 33.80 points at 2,752.55.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended down 16.67 at 3,579.42.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6890 marks and 115.65 yen compared with 1.6918 marks and 113.65 yen in late European trade on Wednesday.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400 GMT
Gold fixed at $342.75 an ounce compared with $342.65 an ounce at Wednesday's close in London.
